c.tagline: Ancient pyramids beside a teeming megacity

taxi.fareNote: white taxis metered but often ignored; agree fare or use apps

emergency.note: Tourist police 126 and fire 180 also work; English-speaking operators are unreliable, so ask hotel staff to call.

hood_landmark.Zamalek: Cairo Tower's 187 m panorama over the Nile
hood_landmark.Maadi: leafy Nile corniche promenade and felucca launches
hood_landmark.Heliopolis: the Baron Empain Palace, a Hindu-style mansion
hood_landmark.Garden City: curving tree-lined streets of colonial villas by the Nile Corniche
hood_landmark.Downtown Cairo: the Egyptian Museum on Tahrir Square

avoid.reason: Persistent touts and camel/"guide" scams at the pyramids and Khan el-Khalili; use official transport.

hood_desc: A leafy, upscale island district in the Nile with embassies, art galleries, cafes and colonial-era buildings; suits first-time visitors and culture lovers wanting a refined, central, walkable base.
A green, tree-lined southern suburb popular with expats, with quiet villas, international schools and cafes; suits families, longer-stay visitors and those wanting calm away from the chaos.
A historic, upscale northeastern district of grand early-20th-century architecture near the airport, with palaces, cafes and shopping; suits travelers wanting elegance and proximity to the airport.
An elegant older riverside district of curving streets, embassies and belle-epoque mansions just south of downtown; suits those wanting a quiet, central, atmospheric base.
The bustling early-modern core with Tahrir Square, the Egyptian Museum, khedival architecture, cafes and street life; suits budget travelers and those wanting to be in the energetic historic heart.
lodging: Four Seasons Hotel Cairo at Nile Plaza

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to sealed bottled water to prevent stomach upset.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable Cairo Metro Card at station kiosks/machines or use paper single-ride tickets; fares are distance-based, roughly EGP 8-25 (~$0.15-0.50). Public buses are paid in cash (EGP) directly to the conductor or driver.
transit.hours: The Metro runs about 5:30am-midnight (later on Thursdays/weekends); buses operate similar daytime hours with sparser late-night service.

food.name: Koshary
food.desc: Egypt's carb-loaded national dish - rice, lentils, pasta and chickpeas under spicy tomato sauce and crispy onions.

places.name: Koshary Abou Tarek
places.note: The multi-story koshary temple with constant queues; Egypt's most famous plate

places.name: Koshary El Tahrir
places.note: Iconic, authentic downtown chain locals rank at the top in 2025 lists

places.name: Zooba
places.note: Modern, traveler-friendly take on street classics, consistently well reviewed

food.name: Ful medames and ta'ameya
food.desc: Slow-stewed fava beans and crunchy fava-bean falafel with baladi bread - the classic Egyptian breakfast.

places.name: Felfela
places.note: Operating since 1959 with proper ful that locals still rate

places.name: Gad
places.note: Hugely popular local chain for ful, ta'ameya and shawarma

places.name: Zooba
places.note: Praised spice mix on the ful and extra-crunchy ta'ameya

food.name: Hawawshi
food.desc: Spiced minced meat baked inside crisp baladi bread - Cairo's favorite savory street pie.

places.name: El Tabei El Domyati
places.note: Old-school institution recommended for hawawshi in recent local guides

places.name: Sobhy Kaber
places.note: Famed grill house whose deliciously spiced hawawshi draws crowds

food.name: Molokhia
food.desc: Silky green jute-leaf stew with garlic and coriander, served over rice with chicken or rabbit.

places.name: Abou El Sid
places.note: Atmospheric Egyptian classic known for molokhia, mahshi and kofta

places.name: Sobhy Kaber
places.note: Its rich molokhia is repeatedly named among the restaurant's best dishes

food.name: Kofta and kebab
food.desc: Charcoal-grilled spiced lamb kofta and kebab skewers, sold by the kilo with bread and salads.

places.name: Abou Shakra
places.note: Grill institution since 1947, still a first stop for kebab and kofta

places.name: Sobhy Kaber
places.note: Locals' pick for generous mixed-grill platters

food.name: Hamam mahshi (stuffed pigeon)
food.desc: Whole pigeon stuffed with spiced rice or freekeh and roasted - a celebrated Cairo delicacy.

places.name: Farahat
places.note: The famous pigeon specialist in the old city, long loved by locals

places.name: Abou El Sid
places.note: Serves a refined version amid classic Egyptian decor

food.name: Sugarcane juice (asab)
food.desc: Freshly pressed sugarcane juice, icy and sweet - Cairo's essential street refresher.

places.name: Farghaly
places.note: Famous juice chain known for asab and its layered mango cocktails

places.name: Street asab shops
places.note: Neon-lit pressing shops on most corners; drink it fresh at the counter

food.name: Karkadeh (hibiscus tea)
food.desc: Deep-red hibiscus infusion, served hot in winter and iced in summer, usually sweetened.

places.name: El Fishawy
places.note: Cairo's most famous cafe, pouring for over 200 years in the bazaar's alleys

places.name: Naguib Mahfouz Cafe
places.note: Comfortable bazaar cafe named for the Nobel laureate, good for karkadeh

food.name: Ahwa (Egyptian coffee)
food.desc: Thick Turkish-style coffee brewed in a kanaka, often scented with cardamom, at a traditional coffeehouse.

places.name: El Fishawy
places.note: The definitive ahwa experience amid mirrors and mashrabiya

places.name: El Horreya Cafe
places.note: Storied high-ceilinged coffeehouse beloved by artists and locals

landmarks: Great Pyramid of Giza
The last surviving Wonder of the Ancient World, its immense scale makes it one of the most photographed monuments on Earth.
Great Sphinx of Giza
The colossal limestone guardian statue with a human head and lion's body is an unmistakable symbol of ancient Egypt.
Egyptian Museum (Cairo)
Home to over 120,000 ancient artifacts including Tutankhamun's treasures, offering unparalleled close-up shots of pharaonic history.
Cairo Citadel of Saladin
A hilltop medieval fortress offering sweeping panoramic views of Cairo's skyline and minarets.
Mosque of Muhammad Ali
Known as the Alabaster Mosque, its Ottoman-style domes and slender minarets crown the Citadel with striking silhouettes at sunset.
Khan el-Khalili Bazaar
A centuries-old labyrinthine market bursting with lanterns, spices, and artisan stalls, ideal for vibrant street photography.
Hanging Church (Coptic Cairo)
One of Egypt's oldest churches, suspended above a Roman gatehouse, with intricately carved wooden screens and icons.
Cairo Tower
A lattice-work tower resembling a lotus flower that offers a striking silhouette and the best rooftop views over the Nile and city.
Al-Azhar Mosque
One of the oldest mosques in Cairo, with a beautiful courtyard and minarets showcasing centuries of Islamic architecture.
Nile Corniche
The riverside promenade along the Nile offers classic golden-hour photos of feluccas sailing against the Cairo skyline.

train.note: Egypt's railways are not connected to any neighbouring country, so there are no international trains. Egyptian National Railways runs the domestic network from Ramses (Cairo) station, including day trains up and down the Nile; overnight sleeper trains to Luxor and Aswan are run by Watania Sleeping Trains and booked separately.

intl.to: Aqaba & Amman (Jordan) - includes the Nuweiba-Aqaba ferry

bus.note: Jordan's national carrier JETT runs a through Cairo-Aqaba-Amman service that bundles the Red Sea ferry crossing into one ticket. Long-distance domestic coaches (Go Bus, Blue Bus, SuperJet) leave from Cairo Gateway (Turgoman) terminal. Overland routes west to Libya and south to Sudan are closed or unsafe.

intl.to: Aqaba (Jordan) - departs Nuweiba port in Sinai, ~7h from Cairo by road

ferry.note: Cairo is inland and has no ferries of its own. The main international sea route is the Nuweiba (Sinai) to Aqaba (Jordan) car and passenger ferry operated by Arab Bridge Maritime, reached by a long road journey across Sinai. The old Lake Nasser ferry from Aswan to Sudan is suspended amid Sudan's conflict.

half.name: Saqqara
half.blurb: Home to the famous Step Pyramid of Djoser, this vast necropolis is one of Egypt's oldest.

half.name: Memphis
half.blurb: The ancient capital of Egypt is now an open-air museum with colossal statues of Ramses II.

half.name: Dahshur
half.blurb: People come for the striking Bent and Red Pyramids, quieter and less crowded than Giza.

half.name: Fayoum
half.blurb: Egypt's largest oasis draws travelers with its lake, desert waterfalls and fossil-rich Valley of the Whales.

half.name: Wadi El Natrun
half.blurb: Ancient Coptic monasteries set in the desert make this a peaceful spiritual and historical escape.

full.name: Alexandria
full.blurb: This breezy Mediterranean port charms visitors with its seaside corniche, ancient library and Greco-Roman history.
